source.title: FailSAE: Towards Interpretable Failure Prediction for Vision-Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Jie-Shu Ma; Zong-Xi Liu; Yi Zhu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Uses SAEs as a tool for failure prediction and interpretation, but does not test superposition or any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper measures SAE latent-direction properties and reports concept analyses. These findings concern SAE representations in VLMs, but do not test the listed toy-model, LLM, or feature-unit claims. General failure-prediction performance results are not included because they do not measure the claim's subject.
record.test_reason: The study uses an SAE on CLIP vision-encoder activations as a tool for failure prediction and concept analysis. Its results are its own method's prediction performance and properties of a failure-aware SAE versus a standard SAE. It does not test whether features are superposed, whether polysemanticity stems from capacity, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. Reporting interpretable SAE directions in CLIP is incidental and not framed as evidence about superposition. The subject is also a VLM vision encoder, not an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that SAE-based failure prediction outperforms the baselines, and that failure-aware training makes latent directions more class-specific. They also conclude that failures involve a shift from class-specific toward ambiguous or style-related concepts. They make no claim about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a three-stage failure-aware SAE training and failure-prediction pipeline on VLM representations, rather than the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that failure-prediction accuracy varies with top-K masking; accuracy rises from K=50 to K=300 and is unstable as K increases further. These are prediction-performance settings, not tests of the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Failure-aware training lowered mean label entropy of SAE directions from 2.598 to 1.955 and made activation more selective. Reconstruction MSE (0.0015 vs 0.0019) and decoder orthogonality (0.39 vs 0.38) changed little.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a supervised task loss to SAE training on CLIP ViT-B/16 makes latent directions more class-specific at little reconstruction cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Human judges found more class-consistent directions in the failure-aware SAE among top-activated directions: 25.5% vs 18.6% at top 5%, and 44.1% vs 23.8% at top 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-aware SAE training raises the share of class-consistent directions among the most strongly activated SAE latents in CLIP.

fits_no_version.finding: Failed predictions activate fewer class-specific and more ambiguous or style-related SAE directions than correct ones, across ID, OOD and ADV errors (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In CLIP ViT-B/16, misclassifications coincide with a shift from class-specific to high-entropy SAE directions.

record.problems: The feature-property comparisons provide no uncertainty estimates or significance tests. The human concept evaluation is qualitative and its judgment criterion is described briefly. Some distributional results are reported only qualitatively from figures. The findings are limited to the tested VLM SAE setting and do not test superposition.
record.rows_left_out: None of the claim-relevant SAE property and concept-analysis results were left out. General failure-prediction performance, ablations, and runtime recovery results were omitted because they do not measure a listed claim version or a related feature-geometry finding.

untested.parts: No toy models, and no test of sparsity, feature count or importance against geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
No LLM, and no analysis of feature spread across neurons. The SAE is used on CLIP but not as evidence of superposition.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicality of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Toy Models of Superposition is cited only in passing, and only as an example of qualitative SAE work. Rows r1, r2, r6 and r7 are own-method comparisons, and r6 and r7 are also selection-based. All rows correctly link to no version. The reader's T4 and uses_without_test classification is confirmed.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-model test or test of how feature count, sparsity, or importance affects overlapping near-orthogonal feature geometry.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from capacity competition or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Studies VLMs rather than LLMs and does not test feature distribution across neurons or establish SAE features as evidence of superposition.
Reports concept interpretability, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.
